newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF pays 91.2 bln yen to private sector in Sept.
newsitem.headline: MOF pays 91.2 bln yen to private sector in Sept.

text.p: The Finance Ministry's (MOF) special foreign exchange account paid out 91.2 billion yen to the private sector in September, MOF data showed on Tuesday.
The account manages Japan's external reserves, the world's largest, which stood at $215.03 billion as of the end of September.

The figure consisted of yen payments from the account to the private sector, comprising commercial banks, foreign central banks, municipal governments, public funds and quasi-governmental organisations.
MOF officials do not comment on details of the payments.
According to bankers, there was almost no trace of dollar-buying intervention for yen this month.
Also in September, MOF appeared to have deposited a substantial amount of dollars, from cash raised through dollar buying intervention, at some commercial banks.
Some banks are facing difficulty in rolling over dollar-based lending necessary for their international operations.
